clue.text: Gallery has some Craig Goldsmith retrospective

indicators.note: a retrospective looks back, so the run of letters is read backwards
only some of the letters of these two names are taken, a run straddling the gap between them

explanation.surface: An art gallery is mounting a retrospective of the work of one Craig Goldsmith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes AIGGOL from craIG GOLdsmith, and 'retrospective' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A loggia is an open-sided gallery or arcade along the side of a building.

clue.text: Crack I discovered on ship

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece found on another sits above it, so the first piece comes first

parts.note: the Roman numeral I stands for one
a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: Someone finds a crack while aboard a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A crack is a joke or wisecrack, and a quick single-sentence joke is exactly that.

clue.text: Upset 'cos Greig works on farm

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone called Greig is upset, because he has to work on a farm.
explanation.walkthrough: Virgil's Georgics are four books of poems about farming, so 'works on farm' means literary works.
explanation.definitionFit: Virgil's Georgics are a set of poetic works about agriculture and farm life.

clue.text: Nanny holding dish out upset religious leader

indicators.note: the nanny word holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: an ayah is a nanny or nursemaid in India

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word reads from the bottom up

parts.note: to dish out is to allot or share out

explanation.surface: A nanny, holding a dish, gets upset with a religious leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns ALLOT into TOLLA, which 'holding' places inside AYAH.
explanation.definitionFit: An ayatollah is a senior Shiite Muslim cleric in Iran.

clue.text: Scraps of food and litter to leave

parts.note: a litter is a brood of young animals, here piglets
to will is to leave something to someone by bequest

explanation.surface: Food scraps and rubbish are left behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Pig swill is kitchen waste and leftover food given to pigs as feed.

clue.text: Smollett character English in principle, Greek, strangely

indicators.note: strangely means in an odd way, so these letters are arranged oddly

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Smollett character is English in principle but strangely Greek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' merely places E among the rest of the fodder; 'strangely' rearranges E plus PRINCIPLE plus GREEK.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobias Smollett's 1751 novel is named after its picaresque hero, the title character.

clue.text: Judge to be affected after drink

indicators.note: the posing word comes after the drinking word

parts.note: to sup is to drink
to pose is to behave affectedly, putting on airs

explanation.surface: A judge turns affected after a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To judge something likely is to suppose it, both meaning to reckon or assume.

clue.text: Man's in this deep

parts.note: Man is the Isle of Man, and deep is a poetic word for the sea, so the clue asks which sea the island lies in

explanation.surface: A man is in deep trouble, or deep thought.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man lies in the stretch of sea between Great Britain and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man sits in the body of water between Britain and Ireland.

clue.text: Fancy Head making impression

parts.note: to fancy something is to like it
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbour Inverness or Dungeness

explanation.surface: A fanciful head is making an impression.
explanation.definitionFit: An impression of a person, such as a portrait, is a resemblance or portrayal.

clue.text: Charming girl talking to Mike?

parts.note: a deb is a debutante, a young society girl
someone speaking into a microphone (mike) is broadcasting, on the air

explanation.surface: A charming girl is chatting to a man named Mike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mike' looks like a man's name; it is a microphone, so talking to it means being on air.
explanation.definitionFit: Debonair means suave, confident and stylishly charming.

clue.text: Left in shade by superior satellite communication

parts.note: U stands for upper-class, the socially superior, in British usage

indicators.note: the letter for left goes inside the colour word

parts.note: pink is a shade of colour

explanation.surface: Someone left in the shade by a superior is out of the loop.
explanation.definitionFit: An uplink is the signal path from a ground station up to a satellite.

clue.text: Keenly contested in ring

definitions.meaning: a fierce, evenly matched fight or argument is described with this informal compound
the phrase imitates the sound of a bell when it is rung

explanation.surface: A bout in a boxing ring is keenly contested.
explanation.definitionFit: The compound describes a closely fought contest and also echoes a pealing bell.

clue.text: Czech extremists lurking in sub in small lake

indicators.note: the extreme letters hide inside the money word

parts.note: a sub is an advance of money, a loan

indicators.note: the extremes of the word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Czech extremists are lurking in a submarine on a small lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sub' suggests a submarine; here it is a subsidy or loan.
explanation.definitionFit: A lochan is a Scottish word for a small loch, that is a little lake or pool.

clue.text: She makes visit that's inspiring work

parts.note: to call is to pay a visit

indicators.note: inspiring means breathing in, so the first piece takes the second inside

parts.note: i.e. stands for id est, that is
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A woman pays a visit that inspires someone's work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She' is a Muse: Calliope, muse of epic poetry, fittingly inspires work.
explanation.definitionFit: Calliope is one of the nine Muses, a female figure, so a pronoun for a woman stands in.

clue.text: Wodehouse penning song — insubstantial source of amusement

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the initials hold the other pieces

parts.note: P.G. Wodehouse, the comic novelist, is known by his initials
a lay is a song or ballad
something insubstantial is thin

explanation.surface: Wodehouse writes a slight song for fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penning' suggests writing; here it means enclosing, so PG wraps round LAYTHIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaything is a toy, something used to amuse oneself.

clue.text: Goddess in ruins appears regularly

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals means every other letter

explanation.surface: A goddess's statue appears regularly among ancient ruins.
explanation.definitionFit: Iris was the Greek goddess of the rainbow and messenger of the gods.

clue.text: Distributed tiling inlaid with a duck design

indicators.note: inlaid means set into a surface, so the letter goes inside the anagram
distributed means spread around, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, the letter O

explanation.surface: Tiles distributed across a floor are inlaid with a picture of a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Distributed' rearranges TILING as INTGLI, 'inlaid with' sets A inside to make INTAGLI, and O follows.
explanation.definitionFit: An intaglio is a design incised or engraved into a surface, as on a gem.

clue.text: Water from needle good for a time

indicators.note: one letter stands in place of another, swapping good in for time

parts.note: to needle someone is to irritate them
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Water drawn from a needle is good for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' puts G in place of a T in IRRITATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To irrigate is to supply land with water, so the two verbs coincide.

clue.text: I claim interest — shilling

parts.note: one's bag is one's interest or speciality, as in 'not my bag'
S was the abbreviation for the shilling, the old British coin worth a twentieth of a pound

explanation.surface: Someone claims interest on a shilling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bags' is British children's slang for staking a claim: 'Bags the front seat!'
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'bags' is a schoolchild's way to stake a claim, an idiom for I claim.

clue.text: It covers soldier's head and shoulders with blood

parts.note: to shoulder a burden is to bear it
blood means family, one's kin

explanation.surface: Something covers a soldier's head and shoulders in blood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head and shoulders' reads as one phrase; the definition stops at 'head'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bearskin is the tall fur cap worn by British guardsmen, covering the head.

clue.text: Game doctor runs a hospital in corrupt city

parts.note: Go is a board game from East Asia
MO is a medical officer, an army doctor
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs, doubled here for the plural

explanation.surface: A game doctor runs a hospital in a corrupt city.
explanation.definitionFit: Gomorrah is the biblical city destroyed with Sodom for its wickedness.

clue.text: Nothing stops Chelsea playing tie

indicators.note: stops means plugs a gap, so the letter goes in the middle
playing suggests the football team, but signals the letters are rearranged

parts.note: O is the round figure for nothing

explanation.surface: Chelsea are held to a nil-nil tie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges CHELSEA as SHELACE, which 'stops' plugs with O.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoelace is a cord used to tie up a shoe.

clue.text: Captain Nemo, say, having change of heart, is perishing

indicators.note: the middle letter of the seven-letter word is changed for another

parts.note: Captain Nemo, commander of the Nautilus, is a hero of a submarine story

explanation.surface: Captain Nemo has a change of heart and is perishing.
explanation.walkthrough: SUB HERO has H as its fourth of seven letters; 'having change of heart' swaps it for Z.
explanation.definitionFit: Perishing in British usage means bitterly cold, below the freezing point.

clue.text: Elbows out a yob keeping doctor back

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so the reversed word holds the doctor
back means the slang word is read in reverse

parts.note: an oik is a British slang word for a lout or yob
MB is a Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A yob with his elbows out is holding a doctor back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns OIK into KIO, and 'keeping' puts MB inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Arms akimbo means hands on hips with elbows jutting outwards.

clue.text: Add comment that's not worried investigators

indicators.note: the word for worried is not there, so it comes out

parts.note: to interpolate is to insert remarks into a text or conversation
ate, as in 'what's eating you', means worried

explanation.surface: Someone adds that the investigators are not worried.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's not worried' removes ATE from INTERPOLATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Interpol is the international police organisation coordinating criminal investigation.

clue.text: Beer available around a camp

indicators.note: the beer word goes round the letter

parts.note: lager is beer that is available on tap everywhere

explanation.surface: Beer is available all around a camp.
explanation.walkthrough: A laager is a South African word for a circular camp of wagons.
explanation.definitionFit: A laager is an encampment fortified by a circle of wagons.

clue.text: Maybe a grand opening for selling underwear

parts.note: a grand is a thousand pounds, K (thousand) nicker (slang for a pound)

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Perhaps a big launch event for selling underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a grand opening' reads as a launch; K is a thousand and nicker is British slang for a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: Knickers are women's or girls' underpants, a British word for underwear.

clue.text: What old Scandinavian rings mean

indicators.note: rings means encircles, so the Scandinavian word goes round the other

parts.note: Norse is the old language and people of Scandinavia
eh is an exclamation asking what was said

explanation.surface: What do old Scandinavian rings signify?
explanation.walkthrough: 'rings' looks like jewellery; it is a verb, so NORSE encloses EH.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-horse town is small and poor, so the phrase means petty, shabby or mean.

clue.text: Keen to travel, holding husband by arm

parts.note: a gun is a firearm

indicators.note: the travelling word holds the letter inside

parts.note: to go is to travel

explanation.surface: Keen to travel, a woman holds her husband by the arm.
explanation.definitionFit: Gung-ho means wildly enthusiastic and eager, especially for a fight.
